name: table-count
description: Number of Drizzle pgTable() definitions across shared/. The mature-machine north star is a SMALLER schema (<=450 tables); today's count is far above it. This strict down-only ratchet makes the schema monotonic: adding a table fails CI until the baseline is deliberately bumped (a conscious 'yes we need this'), and every consolidation lowers the baseline toward the target. Founder-chosen 'strict' 2026-07-16.
lastBumpNote: 750 -> 751 on 2026-08-17: `opportunities` -- the Reality Graph's first canonical object (shared/schema/opportunity.ts, migrations/0237_opportunities.sql). THE CONSCIOUS 'YES WE NEED THIS' IS ALREADY ON RECORD: shared/architecture/canon.ts carried `opportunity` with status ABSENT and disposition BUILD, and this migration executes that recorded disposition rather than inventing a new one. THE ABSENCE WAS VISIBLE IN LIVE CODE, NOT ONLY IN PROSE -- which is the test §0 of the campaign directive demands before acting on any written claim: shared/economics/scenario.ts declares SCENARIO_SUBJECT_TYPES as [property, opportunity, deal] and shared/decisions/snapshot.ts declares DECISION_SUBJECT_TYPES as [property, deal, opportunity], so TWO already-canonical tables accepted a subject id that pointed at no table at all; and server/services/decisions/decisionStore.ts:102 resolved an `opportunity` subjectId AS a `properties.id` (`input.subjectType === 'property' || input.subjectType === 'opportunity'` -> resolveSubject(org, 'property', input.subjectId)) for want of any other id space it could belong to. The two subject types were the same rows wearing different labels, so a decision recorded against an opportunity froze another entity's evidence. IDENTITY AND LIFECYCLE ONLY: no score, price, margin or ROI column. `scenarios` owns the arithmetic, `decision_snapshots` the choice, `outcomes` the result -- all three already canonical and all three already accepting an opportunity subject. Duplicating any of them would give one number two owners (canonical law 8). NOT A SECOND HOME FOR AN EXISTING CONCEPT, checked against code rather than assumed -- this is the exact mistake canon.ts had just been CORRECTED for on `parcel`, where canon claimed identity was ABSENT when it already had TWO owners and a third table would have made it worse. `opportunity_scores` is the nearest existing table and is genuinely opportunity-flavoured (org-scoped, opportunity_type, a lifecycle status, keyed by apn/county/state), but its writer AcquisitionRadar.saveOpportunityScore (server/services/acquisitionRadar.ts:827) matches on (organization_id, apn, county, state) with NO opportunity_type in the predicate and UPDATEs opportunity_type in place: one parcel gets exactly ONE row whose kind is overwritten on each rescoring, which is the precise inability BI93 names. Its vocabulary is acquisition-side signal only, its payload is score-shaped, and it keys on `parcel.apn || ''` so every unknown-APN parcel in an org collides on the empty string. CONSOLIDATION IS THE END STATE -- opportunity_scores should become scoring ABOUT an opportunity and shed its status/opportunity_type -- but that rewrites a live radar surface and is deliberately NOT attempted here, so this bump is +1 and not +1-1. THE NATURAL KEY IS THE ParcelRef TRIPLE (parcel_state, parcel_county, parcel_apn), not a properties.id: an opportunity by definition precedes the commitment that would create a property row, and a properties.id would re-conflate the identity shared/parcel/parcelRef.ts had just separated. NO CONVENIENCE FOREIGN KEYS (BI184): no lead_id, property_id or deal_id -- those edges belong to the still-absent Relationship object, and expressing every new edge as a convenience FK is why role-specific tables keep multiplying. REGISTERED in scripts/migrate.mjs, unlike 0236: the distinction is the verb, not the proximity -- 0236 is a destructive DROP held for founder inspection, this is an idempotent CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS, and withholding it would leave shared/schema.ts exporting a table with no relation behind it. PRIOR NOTE -- 763 -> 750 on 2026-08-16: founder ruling (picker) "Triage 3 ways, drop only experiment residue". Thirteen CLASS A tables — storage left behind by modules the deletion ledger ALREADY records as killed, holding no customer content — had their pgTable definitions removed and are dropped by migrations/0236_drop_experiment_residue_tables.sql: agent_improvement_plans, agent_synergy_map, playbook_evolutions, compass_recommendations, spend_watchers, spend_optimizations, causal_investigations, delegated_goals, external_intelligence, product_specifications, build_buy_decisions, feature_impact_scores, automation_executions. A deletion, not a design improvement — the cheapest way to satisfy any of these gates. THE MIGRATION IS NOT APPLIED: a production DROP TABLE is a founder-only hard stop and this session has no DATABASE_URL. Scope was checked rather than trusted: none of the 22 CLASS B tables (customer or regulated records) appears in the migration, and three class-A-by-content tables were deliberately HELD — agent_playbooks (live FKs from institutional_patterns and signal_correlations), scp_evolution_metrics (an unused import in scpGoldenSuite.ts would break the build), and one more recorded in the ledger. Full 48-table triage in docs/company/deletion-ledger.md. Locked in per this ratchet's strictly-down rule. PRIOR NOTE — 761 -> 763 on 2026-08-13: va_tasks + va_sops -- the VA subsystem's persistence layer, built on an explicit founder ruling (BLOCKERS B9; the founder's picker answer names 'real tables + migration for VA tasks and the SOP library, wired to the existing routes'). That ruling IS the conscious 'yes we need this' this ratchet asks for. WHAT WAS THERE: services/vaManagement.ts declared its storage as two string constants -- VA_TASKS_KEY and SOP_LIBRARY_KEY -- and never read either. createTask was a PURE FUNCTION that stamped an id onto its input and returned it, so POST /api/va/tasks answered 200 with a record that existed only in that response; /api/va/metrics and /api/va/audit-trail computed over organizations.settings.va_tasks, an array with NO CREATOR anywhere in the repository, and returned zeros that READ AS MEASUREMENTS; POST /api/va/tasks/:id/verify read-modify-wrote that same array and could never find a task in it. NOT THE SETTINGS BLOB IT WAS AIMED AT: that column is read on nearly every org-scoped request, so an unbounded task history there grows the hot path for every user forever, and concurrent writers clobber each other -- the verify handler already carried a comment recording that exact bug being fixed once with jsonb_set. TWO TABLES AND NOT ONE: DEFAULT_SOPS stays a code constant (AcreOS's own procedure catalogue, versioned with the code that references it); va_sops holds what an ORG writes. Merging them would make a code change look like a customer edit. NOT DEFERRED TO A JSONB COLUMN ON organizations: tasks are a queryable, filterable, paginated collection with per-row lifecycle and per-row verification -- the thing a table is. Both are wired on arrival: GET/POST /api/va/tasks, GET /api/va/tasks/:id, PUT /api/va/tasks/:id, GET/POST /api/va/sops, plus the three existing read routes now reading the table. Recurring tasks were deliberately NOT built -- a schedule table with no runner would be the built-but-unwired defect this repo keeps finding, so GET /api/va/scheduled refuses with 501 instead. PRIOR NOTE -- 760 -> 761 on 2026-08-12: outcomes -- the learning layer, closing the canonical loop (BI1, AA8, canonical law 9). decision_snapshots froze what was KNOWN and PREDICTED and scenarios froze the ARITHMETIC; nothing recorded what the world then DID, so an investor's own history was a pile of forecasts nobody ever graded. AA8 names the Decision->Outcome graph as a compounding moat precisely because a competitor can copy a screen but not a customer's calibration. VARIANCE IS NOT A COLUMN: it is computed as a pure projection over the scenario references the decision already froze, because a stored variance is a third number that can drift from the two it derives from, and improving it later would silently restate how good a past decision looked. decision_snapshot_id IS a real foreign key, unlike the deliberately unconstrained subject_id on evidence_claims / decision_snapshots / scenarios -- those must SURVIVE their subject, whereas an outcome without its decision is meaningless: there is nothing to compare it against and nothing it can teach. The FK is correct here for exactly the reason it was wrong there. NOT REUSING outcome_telemetry (shaped around AGENT performance -- agentActions, messagesSent, responseTime -- and carrying no decision reference) or outcome_calibrations (keyed by agent codename): both are the agent/founder learning loop, and BI76 is explicit that these are different things that must not collapse into one log. BI178 is honoured in the projection: an outcome is an OBSERVATION of what happened, not retroactive validation of the decision, so describeVariance never says a decision was good or wrong -- a record that scores decisions by their results teaches an investor to be lucky rather than right.
minimaNote: VACUITY FLOOR on the SCAN POPULATION, not a ratchet. baselineCount above counts BAD THINGS FOUND, so a scan that stops seeing files finds zero and reports it as progress: a zero baseline PASSes on an empty file set, and a nonzero one prints a stale-high "lock it in" for a number that was never true. MEASURED 2026-08-16: this config matched 158 file(s) (shared/**/*.ts minus tests). Floor set to 120, comfortably below that, so a broken glob or walk trips it while ordinary deletion does not. Checked BEFORE the baseline comparison by scripts/ratchet.mjs; a MISSING floor fails as loudly as a breached one. If a real deletion wave shrinks this population, lower the floor in the same commit and name the wave here — never raise it to silence something, never delete the key. Re-measure with `node scripts/ratchet.mjs --measure`.
